note: DEV-ONLY proxy constants for the per-round loop. These are BAKED here (root:root 0600, unreadable by the solver's dropped uid) and are read from THIS FILE ONLY. They are NOT read from the environment, because the loop engine runs in the solver-writable session shell and anything it reads from env is attacker-controlled. This file contains NO calibrated anchor (baseline_bpb), NO ref_speedup, and NO held-out corpus: the per-round signal is an ABSOLUTE public-proxy val_bpb, never normalised against the graded anchor. The graded score is produced after the session by the runner from a freshly-uploaded /tests over the HIDDEN test split; this loop only decides WHICH snapshot is graded.
dev_train_tokens_note: the per-round proxy trains the candidate recipe on a SMALL public token budget (3M vs the graded 24M), sliced deterministically from the PUBLIC /data/datasets/wikitext_bpe8k/train.bin the solver already has. The budget is TOKENS, not wall-clock, so the resulting val_bpb is a stable function of the recipe+data+seed and is IMMUNE to node speed (a fast node and a slow node consume the same tokens and produce ~the same model); this is the property that makes a stable per-round dev signal achievable for this task and not for its wall-clock siblings.
dev_seed_note: a FIXED dev seed distinct from every graded seed (1337/2027/90101) so the proxy cannot be seed-matched to the grade.
dev_guard_note: wall-clock FEASIBILITY GUARD for the proxy training only, set generously relative to the 3M dev token budget so even a slow node finishes the dev tokens BEFORE the guard fires — this is what keeps the signal node-speed-immune. Enforced by an external setsid process-group kill, never a cooperative in-loop timer.
dev_param_note: the SAME [floor, cap] the graded scorer re-counts. Enforced in the per-round self-check ON PURPOSE, so the public proxy does NOT coach the solver toward a sub-floor 'shrink to the parameter floor' model that the graded scorer would still reject. (Task-design residual: at a 24M-token budget shrinking toward the 20M floor is itself a real source of reward. Enforcing the same floor in the dev proxy keeps the loop from actively teaching that exploit, but does not remove it from the graded reward surface.)
dev_uid_note: the candidate's per-round proxy training runs as uid 65534 (nobody), NOT root — the SAME privilege drop the graded path uses. Kept for the loop for two reasons: (1) fidelity, so the proxy trains under the same constraints as the grade; (2) hardening, so the loop engine (which runs in the solver-writable shell) cannot be turned into a root-training oracle. Set to null to disable (NOT recommended). The child reports the euid it actually ran under.
